v.text: One January day, a wind warmed Calgary by thirty degrees in four hours.
v.said: One January day, a wind warmed Calgary by thirty degrees in four hours.
v.heard: One January day, a wind warmed Calgary by 30 degrees in four hours.

v.text: It's called a chinook. It usually begins with a sudden shift in the wind over the Pacific.
v.said: It's called a shinook. It usually begins with a sudden shift in the wind over the Pacific.
v.heard: It's called a Chinook. It usually begins with a sudden shift in the wind over the Pacific.

v.text: Forced up over the Rockies, the air cools about half a degree for every hundred metres it climbs.
v.said: Forced up over the Rockies, the air cools about half a degree for every hundred metres it climbs.
v.heard: Forced up over the Rockies, the air cools about half a degree for every hundred meters it climbs.

v.text: Then it races down the other side, warming about one degree every hundred metres. Warm, dry wind pours onto the prairie.
v.said: Then it races down the other side, warming about one degree every hundred metres. Warm, dry wind pours onto the prairie.
v.heard: Then it races down the other side, warming about one degree every hundred meters. Warm, dry wind pours onto the prairie.

v.text: You can spot it in the sky: a band of cloud parallel to the mountains, with a sharp, straight edge. The chinook arch.
v.said: You can spot it in the sky: a band of cloud parallel to the mountains, with a sharp, straight edge. The shinook arch.
v.heard: You can spot it in the sky. A band of cloud parallel to the mountains with a sharp, straight edge. The Chinook Arch.

v.text: On January eleventh, nineteen eighty-three, Calgary went from minus seventeen to plus thirteen in four hours.
v.said: On January eleventh, nineteen eighty-three, Calgary went from minus seventeen to plus thirteen in four hours.
v.heard: On January 11, 1983, Calgary went from minus 17 to plus 13 in 4 hours.

v.text: A chinook can even split the map. At seven in the morning on November twenty-second, twenty seventeen, Calgary's airport read minus eight point one. Springbank Airport, just twenty-five kilometres west, read plus eight point four.
v.said: A shinook can even split the map. At seven in the morning on November twenty-second, twenty seventeen, Calgary's airport read minus eight point one. Springbank Airport, just twenty-five kilometres west, read plus eight point four.
v.heard: A Chinook can even split the map. At 7 in the morning on November 22, 2017, Calgary's airport read minus 8.1. Springbank Airport, just 25 kilometers west, read plus 8.4.

v.text: An Environment Canada meteorologist put it at about twenty-five chinook days a winter in Calgary. About one every three or four days.
v.said: An Environment Canada meteorologist put it at about twenty-five shinook days a winter in Calgary. About one every three or four days.
v.heard: An Environment Canada meteorologist put it at about 25 Chinook days, a winter in Calgary. About one every three or four days.

v.text: The name comes from the Chinook people of the lower Columbia River, near the Pacific. But it's also known by an Indigenous name: the snow eater.
v.said: The name comes from the Shinook people of the lower Columbia River, near the Pacific. But it's also known by an Indigenous name: the snow eater.
v.heard: The name comes from the Chinook people of the Lower Columbia River, near the Pacific. But it's also known by an indigenous name, the Snow Eater.

v.text: It melts snow and dries the soil. Trees can start growing too early, and new leaves may be killed by the next frost.
v.said: It melts snow and dries the soil. Trees can start growing too early, and new leaves may be killed by the next frost.
v.heard: It melts snow and dries the soil. Trees can start growing too early, and new leaves may be killed by the next frost.

v.text: Not everyone loves it. In a study published in two thousand, University of Calgary researchers looked at the diaries of seventy-five migraine patients. For some, migraines were more likely just before a chinook, or on high-wind chinook days. Most weren't affected by either.
v.said: Not everyone loves it. In a study published in two thousand, University of Calgary researchers looked at the diaries of seventy-five migraine patients. For some, migraines were more likely just before a shinook, or on high-wind shinook days. Most weren't affected by either.

v.text: A few hours or days later, the cold comes back.
v.said: A few hours or days later, the cold comes back.

v.text: For most people, it's a welcome break from the winter cold.
v.said: For most people, it's a welcome break from the winter cold.
